Why should the wire be checked in a blank flame before a lithium sample is added?
A. It confirms the later sample colour
B. It detects contamination on the wire

Why can sodium contamination obscure another flame-test colour?

parts.prompt:
Why is red litmus dampened for an ammonia gas test?
A. Water alone makes the paper alkaline
B. Dissolved ammonia creates the alkaline conditions
C. Gas displaces water from the litmus
D. Dampness changes nitrogen gas to ammonia
parts.canonical_answer:
B. Dissolved ammonia creates the alkaline conditions. The damp indicator responds to the aqueous alkaline condition.
Distractor explanations: A: Water alone does not create the alkaline response. C: Ammonia dissolves in the moisture rather than merely displacing it. D: Dampness does not convert nitrogen gas into ammonia.
marking_guidance: Correct option B (1). B. Dissolved ammonia creates the alkaline conditions. The damp indicator responds to the aqueous alkaline condition. Distractor explanations: A: Water alone does not create the alkaline response. C: Ammonia dissolves in the moisture rather than merely displacing it. D: Dampness does not convert nitrogen gas into ammonia. No mark for more than one selected option.
